title: Omophorion
html_source:
“Omophorion” is the Greek word for a cape-like garment worn by the bishop of the orthodox church on his shoulders (omos=shoulder, phero=bear, therefore omophorion=borne on the shoulders).

It is usually made of sheep’s wool in reference to the parable of the good shepherd that held the sheep on his shoulders to save it. It ties in with the “mitre” and “crozier” mentioned in the same sentence which are also parts of the bishop’s attire.
